subject: R shiny leaflet maps do not load for more than one browser instance

messages.author: 18544164dc10c6b7
messages.subject: R shiny leaflet maps do not load for more than one browser instance
parts:
We're creating a webapp (http://52.2.13.97:3838/Boston-Inspections/) that uses a `leaflet` map. `shiny-server` is being run on an Amazon EC2 Ubuntu instance. The code for the webapp can be found on the github: https://github.com/jkgenser/Boston-Inspections

We noticed (and you can probably notice from the link) that the map does not update as it should when the `shiny` inputs change. However, they do update for the very first instance of `shiny` on the EC2 instance.

Does anyone know why the map would properly render for the very instance, but for every subsequent instance, the map simply does not load/update? If it helps, all of these 'instances' seem to run in the same worker process on the EC2 instance (ie. multiple tabs running the webapp will all be contained under the same process via `ps aux`). We suspect it might have something to do with leaflet only rendering once per shiny process, so when one user controls that process, they control the rendering but no other user who opens the webapp can have their leaflet map re-render and update. We’d greatly appreciate if you have any insight into this.

Thanks for any insights you can offer!

On Thu, Sep 10, 2015 at 3:25 AM Huidong TIAN <tienh...@gmail.com> wrote:
Interesting shiny app! I found the map updates in Google Chrome.


On Wednesday, September 9, 2015 at 11:13:40 PM UTC+2, Alex Petralia wrote:
We're creating a webapp (http://52.2.13.97:3838/Boston-Inspections/) that uses a `leaflet` map. `shiny-server` is being run on an Amazon EC2 Ubuntu instance. The code for the webapp can be found on the github: https://github.com/jkgenser/Boston-Inspections

We noticed (and you can probably notice from the link) that the map does not update as it should when the `shiny` inputs change. However, they do update for the very first instance of `shiny` on the EC2 instance.

Does anyone know why the map would properly render for the very instance, but for every subsequent instance, the map simply does not load/update? If it helps, all of these 'instances' seem to run in the same worker process on the EC2 instance (ie. multiple tabs running the webapp will all be contained under the same process via `ps aux`). We suspect it might have something to do with leaflet only rendering once per shiny process, so when one user controls that process, they control the rendering but no other user who opens the webapp can have their leaflet map re-render and update. We’d greatly appreciate if you have any insight into this.

Thanks for any insights you can offer!

We're very interested in tracking down the issue with Shiny Server though. Could you start by upgrading to the 1.4 release of Shiny Server? https://www.rstudio.com/products/shiny/download-server/

On Sat, Sep 12, 2015 at 12:34 PM Alex Petralia <alex.p...@gmail.com> wrote:
Yes actually, in several browsers. 

We were able to get the app to work using a shinyapps.io server: https://jgenser.shinyapps.io/Boston-Inspections

This of course means it was a server issue. It wasn't in the main log files but perhaps elsewhere. Thanks for your help however!

On Fri, Sep 11, 2015 at 6:29 PM, Winston Chang <win...@rstudio.com> wrote:
Alex, I haven't been able to reproduce the problem when I visit your app with four cocurrent sessions. Is the problem still happening for you?

-Winston

On Thu, Sep 10, 2015 at 1:49 PM, Alex Petralia <alex.p...@gmail.com> wrote:
Nope no interesting logs.. just attaching packages and this (which is the same warning we see locally): Assuming 'Longitude' and 'Latitude' are longitude and latitude, respectively

We thought it was a performance issue but the same problem persisted when upgrading to t2.large (we're on t2.medium) now. It's possible we'd need an even more powerful ec2 instance but the process only runs at like 2-5% of CPU.

I've uploaded the file to my Google Drive here: https://drive.google.com/open?id=0B7PvXX3ohFgGamZKRGwzY0FGWHc (if there's a safer way to upload it like a pastebin, please let me know. I tried but 48MB was too large for pastebin)

On Thu, Sep 10, 2015 at 1:20 PM, Joe Cheng <j...@rstudio.com> wrote:
Also, are there any interesting logs under /var/logs/shiny-server/ at the time when you see this problem? (When you close the browser window that is exhibiting the problem, the server may delete the relevant log file.)

I'm not seeing the problem on all-but-the-first-session, it appears to be random for me, with it working more often than not. But if a session exhibits the problem, that session does appear "stuck" in that state.
